units.title: The Nature of Management
units.unit_introduction: Management is the process of coordinating resources and people to achieve organizational goals. This chapter introduces the meaning, functions, levels, and roles of managers.
unit_objectives: Define management and explain efficiency and effectiveness.
Identify the four core management functions.
Describe the responsibilities of managers at different organizational levels.

topics.title: Meaning and Purpose of Management

key_concepts.details: Management involves planning, organizing, leading, and controlling human, financial, physical, and information resources to achieve objectives.
Efficiency concerns using resources wisely with minimal waste; effectiveness concerns achieving the intended goals. Successful management requires both.

activities.description: Choose a local business and identify one example of efficiency and one example of effectiveness.

topics.summary: Managers coordinate resources to accomplish goals efficiently and effectively.

topics.title: Functions and Levels of Management
objectives: Explain planning, organizing, leading and controlling.
Differentiate top, middle and first-line management.

key_concepts.details: Planning sets objectives and determines actions; organizing assigns resources and responsibilities; leading motivates and guides people; controlling compares results against plans and corrects deviations.
Top managers set broad direction, middle managers translate strategy into departmental plans, and first-line managers supervise day-to-day operations.

activities.description: Draw a simple organizational chart for a business and assign a management function to each level.

topics.summary: The management functions operate at all levels, but responsibilities vary.

units.unit_summary: Management combines goal achievement with responsible use of resources through planning, organizing, leading and controlling.

units.title: Planning and Decision Making
units.unit_introduction: Planning gives organizations direction by identifying objectives and selecting actions. Decision making supports managers in choosing among alternatives.
unit_objectives: Describe the purpose and stages of planning.
Differentiate strategic, tactical and operational plans.

topics.title: Planning and Types of Plans
objectives: Distinguish strategic, tactical and operational planning.

key_concepts.details: Managers analyze the situation, set measurable objectives, identify alternatives, select actions, allocate resources, and monitor outcomes.
Strategic plans establish long-term direction; tactical plans translate strategy into departmental actions; operational plans define specific short-term tasks.

activities.description: Write one SMART objective and a three-step action plan for a student project.

topics.summary: Effective planning connects objectives to resources, actions, and evaluation.

topics.title: Managerial Decision Making

key_concepts.details: Define the problem, establish criteria, generate alternatives, evaluate options, select an option, implement it, and review results.
Managers often make decisions with limited time, incomplete information, and cognitive constraints; therefore, they may choose satisfactory rather than optimal solutions.

activities.description: Compare two possible solutions to a campus service problem using cost, time and expected benefit as criteria.

topics.summary: Structured decision making improves transparency and consistency.

units.unit_summary: Planning establishes objectives and action paths, while decision making selects workable alternatives.

units.title: Organizing and Organizational Structure
units.unit_introduction: Organizing arranges people, tasks and resources so that plans can be implemented. Organizational structure clarifies authority, accountability and coordination.
unit_objectives: Explain division of work, departmentalization and delegation.
Compare centralized and decentralized decision making.
Identify strengths and limitations of common organizational structures.

topics.title: Principles of Organizing
objectives: Describe delegation and span of control.

key_concepts.details: Specialization assigns tasks according to skills and expertise, potentially improving productivity while requiring coordination.
Delegation assigns authority and responsibility for tasks while the manager remains accountable for overall results.
Span of control is the number of employees directly reporting to a manager; the appropriate span depends on task complexity and staff capability.

activities.description: Design roles for a five-person project team and show who is responsible for each task.

topics.summary: Organizing clarifies responsibilities and supports coordination.

topics.title: Organizational Structures

key_concepts.details: Employees are grouped by specialist activities such as finance, marketing and operations. This supports expertise but may create coordination barriers.
Activities are grouped by product, region or customer group, improving local responsiveness but potentially duplicating resources.
Centralization concentrates decisions at higher levels; decentralization distributes authority closer to operational teams.

activities.description: Compare functional and divisional structures for a company operating in three regions.

topics.summary: Structure should reflect strategy, size, environment and coordination needs.

units.unit_summary: Effective organizing matches roles, authority and structure to organizational objectives.
